business.body:
- "Thermax at a Glance" states Revenue Rs.10,694 crore, "Installations in 90+ Countries", "Sales and Service Presence in 30+ Countries" and 9,291 employees globally (including permanent employees, FTCs and permanent workers). The deck does not label the period for the Rs.10,694 crore revenue figure.
- Tagline throughout is "Conserving Resources, Preserving the Future", with the business framed around sustainable energy and environment solutions rather than conventional capital goods.
- Reported through four segments — Industrial Products, Industrial Infra, Green Solutions and Chemicals — with subsidiaries TBWES (boilers) and TOESL (build-own-operate green steam/utilities) named as distinct delivery vehicles.
- "Data centres are gaining traction as a high-potential growth sector", and industry outlook adds "Data center investment is accelerating, reinforcing demand for reliable power, cooling, and efficiency solutions."
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order-book methodology change] "During the year, TOESL adopted a rolling 12-month forecast model for reporting its order book, replacing the earlier practice of reporting only the first year's revenue from long-term contracts that typically run for around 10 years. As a result of this methodological change, the reported order book increased by Rs. 139. This adjustment does not impact underlying contracts, revenue recognition, or financial results." (The deck prints "Rs. 139" without a unit; the slide's note states values are in Rs. crore.) Green Solutions order booking growth of 149% therefore blends genuine improvement at TOESL with this reporting change.
- [Project cost overrun] "The lower profit for the quarter was predominantly due to the one project cost overrun of Rs. 91 crore recognised in the Industrial Infra segment", described elsewhere as "a Rs. 91 crore increase in the estimated cost to complete provision for a specific project in the Industrial Infra Segment, arising from events identified during the quarter." The Green Solutions business separately incurred project overrun costs during the quarter.
- [Demand softness] "Order booking and backlog in the Industrial Infra Segment has declined, primarily due to lower demand" — stated despite the same deck showing Industrial Infra order balance up 31% YoY, a contradiction left as printed.
- [Macro] India's Manufacturing PMI stayed above the 50 expansion mark through Q1 FY27 (54.7 April, 55.0 May, 54.2 June), while "West Asia conflict continues to dampen trade sentiment and regional capex, indicating softer near-term momentum in the Middle East"; Middle East supply chain disruptions are also cited against the resin business.
- [Filing status] This is a "Revised Investor Presentation" for Q1 FY 2026-27, filed July 31, 2026, "incorporating certain updates/modifications" to an earlier submission.

open.item: Company had contracted capital expenditure of Rs. 633.89 crore remaining to be executed on capital account, net of advances, as at March 31, 2026 (per the page-165 capital-commitments note).
A separate capital-commitments note (page 225) discloses Rs. 46.21 crore of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account, net of advances, as at March 31, 2026.

Board recommended an aggregate final dividend of Rs. 20 per equity share (Rs. 14 final + Rs. 6 special dividend marking the 60th anniversary), i.e. 1,000% of face value, for FY2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.
open.promised: Rs. 20 per share INR per share

open.item: Company is looking to establish India's first green methanol facility at Deendayal Port, Kandla, Gujarat, converting agricultural waste and local biomass into cleaner shipping fuels.

Boards of step-down subsidiaries Jalansar Wind Energy Private Limited and Kanakal Wind Energy Private Limited approved a Scheme of Amalgamation under Section 233 of the Companies Act, 2013 (Feb 4, 2026 board meetings), subject to receipt of necessary approvals; on effectiveness, Kanakal will issue one equity share for every share held in Jalansar.

Following four fatalities during the year, the Board has discussed a fundamental reassessment of Thermax's safety governance structure at the leadership level, in addition to continuous safety training.

First Energy Private Limited (FEPL), the 100% green-power (solar/wind) subsidiary, has not performed as planned; Company is implementing corrective measures to strengthen execution and improve delivery timelines.
Thermax Bioenergy Solutions Private Limited (TBSPL), the bio-CNG business, is in the process of commissioning and handing over plants across India.
Industrial Products business is expanding its international footprint with targeted growth in Southeast Asia, Latin America and other emerging markets.
Scaling gaseous scrubbing offerings for solar, semiconductor and waste-to-energy applications to address evolving environmental compliance needs.

Board approved a Scheme of Merger by Absorption of Buildtech Products India Private Limited into Thermax Limited (Board meeting October 17, 2025), with appointed date April 01, 2025, subject to necessary approvals.
Thermax is developing high-efficiency solid oxide electrolyser (SOEC) solutions with Ceres Power, targeting customers with available waste heat or high-temperature industrial processes.

risks.note: Thermax faces intensifying competition from both domestic and international players in the energy and environmental sectors, which may lead to pricing pressures and margin compression.
risks.risk: Intensifying competition in a crowded market

risks.note: Disruptions caused by geopolitical tensions, raw-material price volatility, or logistical challenges can affect production schedules and cost structures; ongoing conflicts (particularly Middle East) have already disrupted trade flows, commodity prices and supply chains and affected businesses dependent on international sourcing and exports to the region.
Shifts in environmental and energy policies, along with stricter regulatory requirements, could increase compliance obligations, raise costs, and affect business operations.
Rapid technological advancements may render current processes or solutions less competitive unless the Company continuously innovates and adapts to emerging trends.

The shift towards electrified and low-carbon technologies driven by climate change may reduce demand for certain conventional fuel-based and thermal solutions, impacting parts of Thermax's existing portfolio.
risks.risk: Energy-transition demand shift away from conventional/thermal solutions

risks.note: Global economic volatility and domestic market fluctuations may affect industrial capital expenditure and reduce demand for large industrial projects.

The Company reported four fatalities across its operations and project sites during the year, reinforcing the need to further strengthen safety ownership, risk controls and behavioural interventions across all levels.

As a net importer of crude oil, India (and by extension Thermax's cost base) remains exposed to global energy-price volatility, while currency market volatility could continue to exert pressure on the Indian rupee and influence input-cost dynamics.
